explanation: The raised ridges of the cerebrum are gyri. The shallow grooves between them are sulci, and the deep grooves are fissures.
The cornea is the clear window at the front of the eye, over the iris and pupil.
The arrow points to the incus (anvil), the middle ear bone. It sits between the malleus, which attaches to the eardrum, and the stapes.
The arrow points to the hypothalamus, the area below the thalamus that controls body temperature, hunger, thirst, and the pituitary gland.
The corpus callosum is the C-shaped band of white matter that connects the right and left cerebral hemispheres.
The eustachian (auditory) tube runs from the middle ear to the throat and equalizes pressure on the eardrum.

explanation: The choroid plexus is the network of capillaries in the ventricles that makes cerebrospinal fluid.
The central canal is the small opening in the middle of the gray matter of the spinal cord. It holds cerebrospinal fluid.
tags: nervous system,brain and senses lab,spinal cord

explanation: The ciliary body is the ridged ring behind the iris. Its muscle changes the shape of the lens to focus.
The lateral white column is the white matter on the side of the spinal cord, between the dorsal and ventral horns of gray matter.
